description: Surviving mutants a maintainer has looked at and accepted: equivalent ones (no input can tell them apart from the original) and ones that only make a check stricter. tests/mutation_check.py leaves these out of its report. An entry matches by module (a measured Python module, or .claude/hooks/gate-git-diff.sh), operator (cosmic-ray's, or one of the bash/ operators tests/mutation_check.py makes for the hook) and the stripped text of the source line, so it follows the line when code above it moves and stops matching when the line itself changes. tests/test_mutation_check.py fails when an entry's line no longer exists. Say in reason why the mutant cannot matter.

accepted.line: '{' | '}' | '!' | '(' | if | then | else | elif | fi | do | done | while | until | time | coproc) ((i++)) ;;
accepted.reason: `}` only closes a compound command, so bash allows no word after it in the same command: a segment that starts with it holds nothing else, and with or without the alternative the pass reads no command in it.

prev_opt is read only in the branch for a wrapper other than env and exec, and the wrapper's name sets it to 0 before that branch runs, so its starting value is never read.
